title: advanceSeries: milestone job is inserted before the series knows about it; a failure in between leaves a live job the series denies exists, or a series that can never advance
detail: advanceSeries() calls insertJob() (which inserts the jobs row, then creates the thread, posts the system message, logs the event and notifies) and only afterwards writes plan[k].job_id and current_index (line 279). Two failure paths: (1) insertJob throws after the jobs row exists (createJobThread, postSystemMessage, logJobEvent or emitMany failing): the catch block (line 282-286) stops the series with 'milestone k+1 could not be created', yet job k+1 exists with series_id/milestone_index set, is listed in GET /v1/jobs, and the seller can accept, deliver and get paid on it while GET /v1/series shows that milestone as 'pending' with job_id null (toSeriesView maps by plan.job_id, not by milestone_index). (2) Process crash between line 277 and 279: current_index stays k, job k+1 exists; when job k+1 completes, finalize -> advanceSeries returns silently at 'idx !== s.currentIndex' (line 246), so the series stays 'active' forever, never creates k+2 and never completes. Same window in createSeries (lines 434-436) for milestone 1's job_id (there the advance still works because current_index is already 1, but the view shows milestone 1 as pending). The 'idempotent via current_index' claim in ADR-33 only holds if the two writes are one unit.
suggestion: Reserve first, insert second: generate the job id up front (newId('job')), do ONE conditional update `UPDATE job_series SET current_index = idx+1, plan = <plan with job_id> WHERE id = ? AND status = 'active' AND current_index = idx` and return if rowsAffected is 0 (already advanced or stopped); then call insertJob with that pre-assigned id. If insertJob throws after the jobs row exists, flip that row to cancelled (setJobIf(id, ['open','quote_requested'], {status:'cancelled', cancelKind:'buyer_withdrew', cancelReason:'platform: milestone could not be created'})) before stopSeriesRow. Independently, make toSeriesView and the 'idx' guard robust: seriesJobs() already returns the jobs, so map them by milestoneIndex (and treat idx > current_index as 'repair: adopt the job and bump current_index') instead of trusting plan.job_id. Add a test that makes createJobThread throw on the second milestone and asserts no orphan open job.

title: Stop-vs-advance race: a milestone can be created after POST /v1/series/{id}/stop, and the stop route promises it cannot
detail: stopSeries() reads the row (active) and does a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='active'. advanceSeries() reads the row (active) at line 243, then awaits several writes in insertJob (line 277), then writes plan/current_index unconditionally (line 279). If the stop lands between line 243 and 277 (a buyer stopping right as auto-complete or its own accept fires; the sweep runs in the same process and interleaves at every await), the series ends 'stopped' AND job k+1 is created as an open job for the seller. The state is at least self-consistent afterwards (current_index and plan are updated, the job is a normal job the buyer can cancel while open), but routes.ts line 148 says 'No further milestone jobs are created' and the ADR says the same, and the buyer who stopped now owns an open order it did not want; if the seller accepts it first the buyer is locked in until the deadline (cannot_cancel_in_progress) and either walks away (recorded on its reputation) or pays.
suggestion: Use the reservation-first conditional update from the previous finding (advance only if status is still 'active' at the moment current_index is bumped); the remaining window is the insertJob duration only. After insertJob, re-read the series once: if status is no longer 'active', cancel the fresh job while it is still open/quote_requested (setJobIf) and emit job.cancelled, so a stop never leaves an unwanted open order. Reword the stop description and how_it_works: 'No milestone is created after this call; a step created in the same instant is cancelled/appears as an open job you can cancel.'

title: Expired-unpaid milestone revived by a late payment: the series is already stopped with 'ended as expired' while the milestone goes on to complete; the sweep note promises a revival the series does not honour
detail: sweepJobs (line 1092-1097) expires an unpaid milestone and calls finalize -> advanceSeries('stopped') -> stopSeriesRow with reason 'milestone k of n ended as expired; nothing further is created'. The thread note posted at line 1095 tells the buyer 'A payment mined within 60 minutes of the deadline still revives the job'. payJob does revive it (status expired -> in_progress/delivered; line 831 only calls recordJobOutcome, not finalize), the buyer accepts, complete() -> finalize('completed') -> advanceSeries returns at 's.status !== active'. End state: series 'stopped' by 'platform' with reason 'ended as expired', milestone k shows status 'completed' and paid=true, totals.completed counts it, and no milestone k+1 is created. Nothing is lost money-wise, but the stated reason is false for the buyer and seller reading the series afterwards, and the buyer paid a late step believing the series continues. Otherwise the terminal mapping matches ADR-33: resolved buyer -> stop, split/seller -> advance, cancelled (walk-away, withdrew, seller_failed, buyer_after_deadline) -> stop, declined/expired -> stop; an open dispute passes finalize without deciding.
suggestion: Cheapest honest fix: in advanceSeries, when outcome==='stopped' and job.status==='expired' && job.unpaid, word the reason 'milestone k of n expired unpaid; a payment in the grace period revives that job but not the series; start a new series for the remaining steps', and append the same sentence to the sweep note at line 1095 when job.seriesId is set. Alternative that honours the promise: do not stop the series on an unpaid expiry while withinGrace(job); stop it from the sweep once paymentDeadlineAt + PAYMENT_GRACE_MS has passed and the job is still expired (query jobs where series_id is set, status expired, unpaid, deadline+grace < now, joined to active series). Pick one and say it in ADR-33.

title: how_it_works and the route text describe the on_delivery flow only; for upfront listings the wording is wrong
detail: HOW says 'the seller accepts, delivers sealed, the buyer pays that step and the output is revealed'. For a listing with payment='upfront' each milestone goes open -> awaiting_payment (buyer pays after acceptance) -> in_progress -> delivered (never sealed) -> completed; the sealed/revealed sentence is false and the buyer is told the wrong moment to pay. The same fixed text is returned for every series and in the GET /v1/series description. The series flow itself handles upfront correctly (insertJob uses listing.payment; sweep expires awaiting_payment; advanceSeries guards payment timing), only the words are off.
suggestion: Make the sentence depend on the listing's payment timing: pass the first job's (or listing's) payment into toSeriesView and render 'the buyer pays that step after the seller accepts, then the seller delivers' for upfront and the sealed/revealed sentence for on_delivery; or phrase it neutrally: 'the buyer pays that step (after acceptance for upfront listings, against the sealed delivery otherwise)'. Add a test that runs a 2-step series on an upfront listing (accept, pay, deliver, accept -> milestone 2 open) and asserts the sentence.

title: Plan size is only bounded by the 1 MB body limit; the full plan (all inputs) is stored per row, rewritten on every advance and returned for up to 100 series per list call
detail: app.ts line 88 sets bodyLimit 1 MB on /v1/*, so one series may carry ~1 MB of milestone inputs (20 x ~50 KB). createSeries stores the whole plan in job_series.plan and each milestone input again in jobs.input; advanceSeries re-serialises and rewrites the whole plan on every step; toSeriesView returns every milestone's full input, and GET /v1/series (routes.ts line 117-118) builds that view for up to limit=100 rows with two extra queries per row (sellersById + seriesJobs), i.e. up to ~100 MB of JSON and 200 queries for one list request. Inputs ARE content-scanned per milestone (validateInput -> scanJson at line 427), so that part is fine.
suggestion: Cap each milestone input (e.g. 64 KB serialised, mirroring the 512 KB output rule) and the whole plan (e.g. 256 KB) in createSeries with a validation error naming milestones[i].input; in the list endpoint return a light view (index, title, units, price, job_id, status, paid) without input, or add ?include=inputs; batch the per-row queries (one sellersById for all rows, one jobs query with inArray(seriesId)).

title: createSeries inserts the series row before milestone 1; if insertJob throws, an 'active' series with no job survives the failed request
detail: Line 433 inserts job_series (status active, current_index 1), then line 434 calls insertJob, which can throw (assertSellerCapacity raced by another order, createJobThread or notify failure). The buyer receives an error and no job, but GET /v1/series lists an active series with every milestone 'pending'; it never advances and cannot be stopped meaningfully (stop works but the row is garbage). Repeating the order creates another one each time.
suggestion: Wrap the insertJob call in try/catch: on failure delete the job_series row (db().delete(jobSeries).where(eq(jobSeries.id, id))) or stopSeriesRow(s, 'platform', 'milestone 1 could not be created (<code>)') and rethrow. Alternatively insert the series row after insertJob succeeds (the id is generated before, and jobs.series_id has no FK), which also removes the plan[0].job_id back-fill at line 436.

title: Per-milestone terms guard covers price and payment timing but not turnaround, accept timeout or input_schema, which are also taken from the CURRENT listing at each step
detail: insertJob copies listing.turnaroundSeconds and listing.acceptTimeoutSeconds at creation, and later milestones are not re-validated against listing.inputSchema. Between steps the seller can PATCH the listing to a 30-day turnaround or a new required key; the next milestone is then created under terms the buyer never saw (the buyer can still cancel while open, or stop the series, but only if it looks). The price/payment comparison itself is correct for fixed, per_unit (price*planned units) and quote (null vs null), and using the previous job's payment as baseline is sound because every step is guarded, so it chains back to step 1.
suggestion: Freeze turnaround_seconds and accept_timeout_seconds on the series row (or per plan entry) at createSeries and pass them into insertJob for milestones; or extend the guard: stop with listing_terms_changed when turnaroundSeconds or acceptTimeoutSeconds differ from the previous job, and re-run the required-keys check of validateInput against the current inputSchema (stop with listing_schema_changed). Say in ADR-33 which terms are frozen.

title: Reputation: a series is N completed jobs and N reviews from one counterparty; not a tier exploit, but jobs_completed / rating_count / rating_avg inflate per step and nothing says so
detail: T1 needs distinct paying addresses (TRUST_T1 minPayingAddresses 3, minCounterparties 3), and weightedRating collapses per reviewer, so a 20-step series with one buyer cannot reach T1 by itself. But jobs_completed (+20), rating_count (+20) and bayesianRating (per review, not per reviewer) all count every milestone, category cards are sorted by jobs_completed, and listing stats count rating_count per review. The test at routes.test.ts line 104 even asserts jobs_completed 3 for one counterparty. The design is defensible (each step is a real delivery and a real payment), but ADR-33 and the reputation docs do not mention it, and a reader of jobs_completed will overcount demand.
suggestion: Add one sentence to ADR-33 and to the reputation section of the API docs: 'every milestone counts as one job and one review; distinct_counterparties and the trust tiers are per wallet, so a series cannot fake breadth'. If ranking by jobs_completed matters, sort category cards by (distinct counterparties, jobs_completed) or expose series_count next to jobs_completed. No code change is required for money or tier safety.

title: Test gaps that guard money or state
detail: Not covered: (1) the per_unit price-change guard (the per_unit test never completes a milestone; only the fixed-price guard is exercised) and the listing_payment_changed guard (never exercised); (2) the stop-vs-advance race (stop issued while the previous milestone is being auto-completed by the sweep); (3) expired-unpaid milestone revived by a late payment (series stopped, job then completes: the assertion of the resulting status/reason); (4) a full quote flow across an advance (quote -> accept_quote -> deliver -> pay -> accept -> milestone 2 quote_requested, price_total following the quoted prices); (5) any upfront-listing series (accept -> awaiting_payment -> pay -> deliver -> accept -> advance; unpaid expiry in awaiting_payment stops it); (6) GET /v1/series pagination: has_more/next_cursor with limit=1 across 3 series, role=buyer|seller filter, a live series id fetched with a test key (404); (7) buyer walk-away on a sealed delivery and seller cancel in_progress after payment (refund_due plus series stopped); (8) seller at max_open_jobs when the next milestone is due (seller_busy stop reason); (9) a failure inside insertJob on milestone 2 (no orphan open job, series stopped once); (10) idempotency of stop with an Idempotency-Key replay; (11) that a bounty-awarded job has series null (createJobFromBountyAward sets no series fields: confirmed by reading, untested).
suggestion: Add one test per gap; (1), (3), (5), (7) and (9) are the ones that touch money or terminal state and should land before the next deploy.

title: Buyer is not told that the seller sees every future milestone input from step 1
detail: toSeriesView returns milestones[].input for all steps to both parties, and the seller learns the series id in the job.created event and the thread system message of milestone 1. Only the GET /v1/series/{id} description says 'The seller sees the whole plan before accepting milestone 1'; the CreateJobRequest.milestones description (the text an agent reads before sending), skill.md step 4 and the MCP create_job description do not. A buyer who plans steps 2..n with information it meant to reveal later sends them without knowing.
suggestion: Append to the milestones description in routes.ts:113: 'The seller sees the whole plan (every step's input) from milestone 1 on and can decline or stop at any step; put into later steps only what the seller may read now.' Add the same sentence (short form) to skill.md step 4 in packages/api/src/discovery/text.ts:82 ('the seller sees every step's input from step 1') and to the milestones .describe() in packages/api/src/mcp/server.ts:135; regenerate the three SKILL.md copies.

title: build.commit can name a commit the image was not built from (dirty or unpushed tree)
detail: The deploy command bakes $(git rev-parse HEAD) into the image, but flyctl uploads the working tree, not the commit. With uncommitted changes (or a commit not yet pushed) GET /health build.commit names public source that differs from what runs, which is exactly the false statement ADR-32 forbids ('Git commit of the public repository the running image was built from'). Nothing in the command or the doc guards against it.
suggestion: In DEPLOY.md require a clean, pushed tree before the deploy and give a one-liner that enforces it, e.g. [ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ] && git fetch -q && [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" ] && flyctl deploy . --remote-only -a agentsouk-api --build-arg GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD); alternatively pass GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)-dirty when the tree is dirty (buildInfo then yields null because of the regex, which is the honest value).

title: HealthSchema.build description claims the running deployment can be 'checked' against the source
detail: The build object description reads 'ties the running deployment to a commit of the public source, so "the source is public" can be checked against what is actually running'. Nothing can be checked: build.commit is a string the operator chose at deploy time (the commit description itself says 'our own statement, not a reproducible build'). The same sentence is in the 0.4.0 changelog (meta/routes.ts:23). Per ADR-32 a capability must carry its limit in the same sentence.
suggestion: app.ts:140: 'ADR-32: names the commit of the public source we say the running image was built from. Our own statement: without a reproducible build nothing proves the image matches it.' meta/routes.ts:23: 'GET /health names the commit the running image was built from (build.commit, build.source) and the container image (build.image). Our own statement, not proof: there is no reproducible build (ADR-32).'

title: 'null when the build was not tagged' is wrong terminology
detail: build.commit is null when the GIT_SHA build arg was not passed (or is 'unknown'/not hex), not when a git tag is missing. Agents read 'tagged' as a git tag.
suggestion: 'null when the image was built without the GIT_SHA build arg (local builds).' Same wording in the config.ts:81 comment.

title: Smoke check accepts only a 40-hex commit while buildInfo accepts 7 to 40 hex
detail: buildInfo() (app.ts:40) passes any 7-40 hex string, so a deploy with --build-arg GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) shows a 7-char commit in /health and a tree link, but the smoke test fails on it. Either both accept short shas or neither.
suggestion: Tighten app.ts:40 to /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/i (a full sha is what the tree link and 'the commit' promise) and keep the smoke regex; or relax smoke to /^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/.

title: paid_total is gross of refunds and ignores partial payments; the description says 'paid'
detail: paid_total sums job.price for every milestone job with paidAt set. A milestone that was paid, disputed, resolved for the buyer and refunded still counts fully; a partial transfer below the price (settlement status 'partial') counts nothing until complete. 'USDC minor units paid on milestone jobs so far' therefore over- or understates what actually moved.
suggestion: Description: 'Sum of the prices of milestone jobs whose payment was verified. Partial transfers below a step's price are not counted until the step is paid; refunds are not subtracted (see each job's payment.refund).' Or compute from settlements: settled amounts minus refunds.

title: stopped_by is a free string in the schema although it is a closed set
detail: stopSeriesRow only ever writes 'buyer' | 'seller' | 'platform', but SeriesView declares z.string().nullable(), so the OpenAPI schema and the SDK types do not tell an agent which values to switch on.
suggestion: stopped_by: z.enum(['buyer', 'seller', 'platform']).nullable().openapi({ description: 'Who ended the series: a party, or the platform when a step failed or the next one could not be created.' })

title: create_job does not say that exactly one of input or milestones is required
detail: Both input and milestones are optional in the tool schema; the description says 'send milestones ... instead of input' but never states that one of them is required, so a model can call with neither and only learn it from the 400. The REST CreateJobRequest refine says it explicitly. The tool also carries the approved limit statement but not the negation used on every other surface.
suggestion: Add to the description: 'Send exactly one of input (one job) or milestones (a series); neither or both is rejected. This limits exposure; it is not buyer protection.'

title: series_action get/stop with a missing id calls GET /v1/series/ and returns a routing 404 instead of a clear tool error
detail: encodeURIComponent(id ?? '') yields '' so the tool requests /v1/series/ (a not_found from the router, not the series 404 with its hint) and POST /v1/series//stop. A model gets 'not found' for what is a missing argument.
suggestion: Before the calls: if (action !== 'list' && !id) return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'id (ser_...) is required for get and stop' }], isError: true } (dispute_action has the same shape; fix both the same way).

title: tools/list expectation does not name series_action
detail: The tool list assertion enumerates the tools the platform advertises; series_action (new in 0.4.0) is not in it, so a regression that drops the tool would pass. Not required by the build, noted as asked.
suggestion: Add 'series_action' to the names array at line 38.

title: The four series events are not named on any discovery surface
detail: series.created/advanced/completed/stopped appear only in the changelog and in the create-job next_steps. The llms.txt Milestones line and skill.md do not name them, so an agent subscribing with event_types cannot know the prefix to use; the payload shape (series_id, listing_id, title, buyer_id, seller_id, count, current_index, status plus job_id/index/previous_job_id/last_job_id/stopped_by/reason) is documented nowhere.
suggestion: Append to the llms.txt Milestones line: '; events series.created, series.advanced (job_id of the new step), series.completed, series.stopped (stopped_by, reason) go to both parties (webhook event_types "series.*")'. Same short clause in skill.md step 4.

title: 'The risk reduction we work on (milestones, ...)' is stale: milestones are built
detail: what_we_do_not_offer[5].meaning still lists milestones as something being worked on, while who_carries_the_risk.milestones and the 0.4.0 changelog present them as live. A reader checking consistency finds the document contradicting itself.
suggestion: 'The risk reduction we offer (milestones, ADR-33) or work on (exposure suggestions) touches no funds.'

title: Changelog 0.4.0 and APP_RELEASED are dated 2026-09-09, one day after the commits
detail: The build commits are dated 2026-09-08 (23:5x local, +0200) and today is 2026-09-08; the changelog entry, APP_RELEASED (version.ts) and ADR-33 say 2026-09-09. If the deploy happens on 2026-09-08 UTC the public changelog carries a future date, and the commitments document uses APP_RELEASED as document_updated.
suggestion: Set the changelog date and APP_RELEASED to the actual deploy day (UTC) at deploy time, or deploy on 2026-09-09 as dated.

title: The disputes doc comment is now orphaned above the series namespace
detail: The series namespace and its own JSDoc were inserted between the multi-line 'Disputes are decided by panels...' comment (lines 578-582) and readonly disputes, so the disputes namespace has no documentation in the generated .d.ts and the dispute text hangs over series.
suggestion: Move the series block (comment plus readonly series = {...}) to after the disputes namespace, or above the disputes doc comment.
